method: Independently downloaded five current-day GitHub Actions ZIPs. Extracted and inspected five review JPGs, all 40 source preview strips (three source time samples each), and 30 actual MP4 narration-block midpoint frames. Probed each complete MP4 with ffprobe; scanned every video with FFmpeg fps=8,scale=320:-2,freezedetect=n=-40dB:d=1.0. Freeze detector flags low-motion, not proven byte-identical still frames. All 5 have audio, 1080x1920 video and 30-45s duration.

findings: Hook alligator small/distant in gray water.
Breathing X-ray block is nearly motionless grayscale, visually unclear in 9:16.
Albino alligator is captive and CC BY-SA 4.0; TikTok ShareAlike compatibility not cleared.
Payoff has egrets and alligators, but subject is too distant for strong storytelling.
First and third scenes are distant nests; actual feeding is not visually demonstrable at midpoint.
Second scene depicts adult bald eagles, not eaglet feeding.
Source 5 and block 5 show a dog on a beach, unrelated to narrated smaller-bird harassment.
Final scene distant bird on a ridge and near-static ending.
Opening digging scene shows a dark bank, not clear digging action at midpoint.
Third narration block shows branches and distant ground instead of visibly entering nest tunnel.
Fifth block claims fishing but image shows a perched bird.
Multiple very low-motion sections including ~5.75s and 5.5s.
Hook mantis is tiny in a busy rocky background, weak leg detail.
Sources 2 and 3 are closely related Flickr mantis-versus-prey footage from same creator; distinct URLs do not establish independent filming.
Block 4 shows a mantis without clear feeding; block 5 shows an ordinary stance rather than unmistakable threat display.
Final frame is a small distant brown mantis on a light background.
Sources 0,1,4 are extremely dark red-lit zoo footage and do not establish the narrated swimming/tail action.
All eight clips are captive Ljubljana Zoo Castor canadensis recordings by the same creator on a small number of dates; do not imply wild filming.
Sources 2,3,5 show swimming or water activity, while 6,7 show close-up feeding/grooming; these do not repair the unusable red clips.
Payoff animal is clearly visible but most early narrative scenes are not.

common_failures: All five current-day MP4s predate the later TikTok attribution renderer: metadata captions have only 73-79 characters and omit source credits. No independent attribution approval.
Rendered metadata lacks explicit publication_hold field; current config still holds all five.
Current configs/daily.json contains numbered placeholder tags for all 30 blocks and sources; newer semantic preflight correctly rejects them.
All five require footage changes, verified descriptive tags, new config push/render, and complete independent audit of new artifacts. Passing CI is not editorial approval.
reason_no_rerender: No fully verified replacement source pools; a speculative rerender would repeat known failures and consume compute.
